claim: The Ska complex is essential for normal anaphase onset in mitosis.
source: The spindle- and kinetochore-associated (Ska) complex is essential for normal anaphase onset in mitosis.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a known fact about the Ska complex.

claim: The C-terminal domain (CTD) of Ska1 binds microtubules.
source: The C-terminal domain (CTD) of Ska1 binds microtubules and was proposed to facilitate kinetochore movement on depolymerizing spindle microtubules.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by citations in the introduction.

claim: The Ska1 CTD was proposed to facilitate kinetochore movement on depolymerizing spindle microtubules.
source: The C-terminal domain (CTD) of Ska1 binds microtubules and was proposed to facilitate kinetochore movement on depolymerizing spindle microtubules.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as a previous proposal about Ska1 CTD function.

claim: The Ska complex recruits protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) to kinetochores.
source: Here, we show that Ska complex recruits protein phosphatase 1 (PP1) to kinetochores.
evidence: This is the main finding stated in the abstract and supported by experimental data throughout the manuscript.

claim: PP1 recruitment by Ska requires the Ska1 CTD.
source: This recruitment requires the Ska1 CTD, which binds PP1 in vitro and in human HeLa cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by multiple experiments showing binding interactions.

claim: The Ska1 CTD binds PP1 in vitro.
source: This recruitment requires the Ska1 CTD, which binds PP1 in vitro and in human HeLa cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by in vitro binding assays and MST experiments.

claim: The Ska1 CTD binds PP1 in human HeLa cells.
source: This recruitment requires the Ska1 CTD, which binds PP1 in vitro and in human HeLa cells.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Ska1 lacking its CTD fused to a PP1-binding peptide rescues mitotic defects caused by Ska1 depletion.
source: Ska1 lacking its CTD fused to a PP1-binding peptide or fused directly to PP1 rescues mitotic defects caused by Ska1 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by live cell imaging experiments.

claim: Ska1 lacking its CTD fused directly to PP1 rescues mitotic defects caused by Ska1 depletion.
source: Ska1 lacking its CTD fused to a PP1-binding peptide or fused directly to PP1 rescues mitotic defects caused by Ska1 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by live cell imaging experiments.

claim: Ska1 fusion to catalytically dead PP1 mutant does not rescue mitotic defects and shows dominant negative effects.
source: Ska1 fusion to catalytically dead PP1 mutant does not rescue and shows dominant negative effects.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated by live cell imaging experiments.

claim: The Ska complex recruits PP1 to kinetochores to oppose spindle checkpoint signaling kinases and promote anaphase onset.
source: Thus, the Ska complex, specifically the Ska1 CTD, recruits PP1 to kinetochores to oppose spindle checkpoint signaling kinases and promote anaphase onset.
evidence: This is the main conclusion stated in the abstract and supported by multiple lines of experimental evidence.

claim: Microtubule binding by Ska may serve to promote PP1 recruitment to kinetochores fully attached to spindle microtubules at metaphase rather than acting in force production for chromosome movement.
source: Microtubule binding by Ska, rather than acting in force production for chromosome movement, may instead serve to promote PP1 recruitment to kinetochores fully attached to spindle microtubules at metaphase.
evidence: This is a proposed model stated in the abstract based on the experimental findings.

claim: Anaphase onset and mitotic exit are driven by proteasome-mediated destruction of Securin and Cyclin B.
source: Anaphase onset and mitotic exit are driven by proteasome-mediated destruction of Securin and Cyclin B, which are targeted for ubiquitylation by the E3 ligase, the Anaphase-promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) (Sivakumar and Gorbsky, 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to support the claim.

claim: APC/C activity is restrained by the spindle checkpoint until metaphase.
source: Until metaphase, APC/C activity is restrained by the spindle checkpoint.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as established knowledge about cell cycle regulation.

claim: A key element in extinguishing checkpoint signaling when chromosomes align at metaphase is the displacement of Mps1 from its substrate, Knl1, at kinetochores.
source: Recent studies indicate that a key element in extinguishing checkpoint signaling when chromosomes align at metaphase is the displacement of the critical checkpoint signaling kinase, Mps1, from its substrate, Knl1, at kinetochores (Aravamudhan et al., 2015; Hiruma et al., 2015; Ji et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to recent studies.

claim: Mps1 phosphorylation events must be reversed by phosphatases to allow anaphase onset and mitotic exit.
source: Then, to allow anaphase onset and mitotic exit, Mps1 phosphorylation events must be reversed by phosphatases.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a logical consequence of checkpoint signaling.

claim: Depletion of the Ska complex leads to a strong metaphase arrest or delay.
source: Previously, we showed that depletion of the Ska complex leads to a strong metaphase arrest or delay (Daum et al., 2009; Sivakumar et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to previous work by the authors.

claim: Cells depleted of the Ska complex exit mitosis more slowly even when Mps1 is directly inhibited with a strong chemical inhibitor.
source: Even when Mps1 was directly inhibited with a strong chemical inhibitor, cells depleted of the Ska complex exited mitosis more slowly (Sivakumar et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to previous work.

claim: The Ska complex plays a role in opposition to, or downstream of, checkpoint signaling.
source: These results suggested that the Ska complex played some role in opposition to, or downstream of, checkpoint signaling.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as an inference from previous experimental results.

claim: PP1 becomes concentrated at kinetochores as chromosomes align to the metaphase plate.
source: As chromosomes align to the metaphase plate, PP1 becomes concentrated at kinetochores stabilizing kinetochore-microtubule interactions, and promoting anaphase onset by opposing spindle checkpoint kinase signaling (Liu et al., 2010; Nijenhuis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: PP1 at kinetochores stabilizes kinetochore-microtubule interactions.
source: As chromosomes align to the metaphase plate, PP1 becomes concentrated at kinetochores stabilizing kinetochore-microtubule interactions, and promoting anaphase onset by opposing spindle checkpoint kinase signaling (Liu et al., 2010; Nijenhuis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: PP1 at kinetochores promotes anaphase onset by opposing spindle checkpoint kinase signaling.
source: As chromosomes align to the metaphase plate, PP1 becomes concentrated at kinetochores stabilizing kinetochore-microtubule interactions, and promoting anaphase onset by opposing spindle checkpoint kinase signaling (Liu et al., 2010; Nijenhuis et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Recruitment of PP1 to the kinetochore leads to substrate dephosphorylation, stabilization of kinetochore-microtubule attachments, and anaphase onset.
source: Recruitment of PP1 to the kinetochore then leads to substrate dephosphorylation, stabilization of kinetochore-microtubule attachments, and anaphase onset (Liu et al., 2010; Nijenhuis et al., 2014; Meadows et al., 2011; Rosenberg et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The heterotrimeric Ska protein complex consists of Ska1–3.
source: The heterotrimeric spindle- and kinetochore-associated (Ska) protein complex consisting of Ska1–3 is required for timely anaphase onset (Daum et al., 2009; Welburn et al., 2009; Gaitanos et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: The Ska complex is required for timely anaphase onset.
source: The heterotrimeric spindle- and kinetochore-associated (Ska) protein complex consisting of Ska1–3 is required for timely anaphase onset (Daum et al., 2009; Welburn et al., 2009; Gaitanos et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Some laboratories have reported that Ska depletion strongly compromises chromosome alignment.
source: Some laboratories have reported that Ska depletion strongly compromises chromosome alignment (Welburn et al., 2009; Gaitanos et al., 2009; Raaijmakers et al., 2009).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to other studies.

claim: Depletion of Ska components, individually or in combination, causes delays in chromosome alignment followed by a robust metaphase arrest.
source: However, our detailed video analyses show that depletion of Ska components, individually or in combination, causes delays in chromosome alignment followed by a robust metaphase arrest (Daum et al., 2009; Sivakumar et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to the authors' previous work.

claim: Metaphase arrest after Ska depletion is often followed by cohesion fatigue and asynchronous chromatid separation without progression to anaphase.
source: Metaphase arrest is often then followed by cohesion fatigue and asynchronous chromatid separation without progression to anaphase (Stevens et al., 2011; Daum et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to support the claim.

claim: Cells that have undergone cohesion fatigue remain arrested in mitosis with a terminal phenotype in which mixtures of separated chromatids and intact chromosomes are scattered across the spindle.
source: Cells that have undergone cohesion fatigue remain arrested in mitosis with a terminal phenotype in which mixtures of separated chromatids and intact chromosomes are scattered across the spindle.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as a description of the phenotype observed after Ska depletion.

claim: The C-terminal domain (CTD) of Ska1 has been termed the microtubule-binding domain or MTBD.
source: The C-terminal domain (CTD) of Ska1 binds to microtubules and has thus been termed the microtubule-binding domain or MTBD (Abad et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to previous structural studies.

claim: HeLa cells expressing Ska1 lacking the CTD showed phenotypes similar to Ska depletion.
source: HeLa cells expressing Ska1 lacking the CTD showed phenotypes similar to Ska depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to previous studies.

claim: Cells expressing Ska1 lacking the CTD delayed at metaphase.
source: Cells delayed at metaphase, and cold stable kinetochore fibers were reportedly decreased (Abad et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to previous studies.

claim: Cold stable kinetochore fibers were reportedly decreased in cells expressing Ska1 lacking the CTD.
source: Cells delayed at metaphase, and cold stable kinetochore fibers were reportedly decreased (Abad et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to previous studies.

claim: In vitro the Ska complex was shown to track depolymerizing microtubule ends.
source: Furthermore, in vitro the Ska complex was shown to track depolymerizing microtubule ends (Schmidt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with a citation to a previous study.

claim: A model has been proposed in which Ska directly promotes microtubule stability and kinetochore movement on microtubules in conjunction with other kinetochore components, such as the Ndc80 complex.
source: These results have led to a model in which Ska directly promotes microtubule stability and kinetochore movement on microtubules in conjunction with other kinetochore components, such as the Ndc80 complex (Abad et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the introduction with citations to previous studies.

claim: Compromising PP1 recruitment by Ska increases phosphorylation of Knl1.
source: Compromising this recruitment increases phosphorylation of Knl1 and increases recruitment of the checkpoint kinase Bub1.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Compromising PP1 recruitment by Ska increases recruitment of the checkpoint kinase Bub1.
source: Compromising this recruitment increases phosphorylation of Knl1 and increases recruitment of the checkpoint kinase Bub1.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Ska1 CTD is required for binding to PP1 in vivo.
source: We find that Ska1 CTD is required for binding to PP1 in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by co-immunoprecipitation experiments.

claim: Ska1 CTD is required for binding to PP1 in vitro.
source: We find that Ska1 CTD is required for binding to PP1 in vivo and in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by in vitro binding assays.

claim: The metaphase arrest or delay seen after Ska depletion is strongly rescued by expressing a chimeric Ska1 protein with its CTD replaced by a PP1-binding motif.
source: The metaphase arrest or delay seen after Ska depletion is strongly rescued by expressing a chimeric Ska1 protein with its CTD replaced either by a PP1-binding motif or by a direct fusion to PP1.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by live cell imaging experiments.

claim: The metaphase arrest or delay seen after Ska depletion is strongly rescued by expressing a chimeric Ska1 protein with its CTD replaced by a direct fusion to PP1.
source: The metaphase arrest or delay seen after Ska depletion is strongly rescued by expressing a chimeric Ska1 protein with its CTD replaced either by a PP1-binding motif or by a direct fusion to PP1.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction and demonstrated by live cell imaging experiments.

claim: A major function of the Ska complex is to recruit PP1 to the kinetochore.
source: Thus, a major function of the Ska complex is to recruit PP1 to the kinetochore.
evidence: This is stated in the introduction as the main conclusion of the study.

claim: The kinetochore levels of PP1 were diminished in Ska3-depleted cells at prometaphase and metaphase.
source: We found that the kinetochore levels of PP1 were diminished in Ska3-depleted cells at prometaphase and metaphase (Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1A with quantification.

claim: The pool of PP1 on the mitotic spindle appeared unaffected by Ska3 depletion.
source: In contrast, the pool of PP1 on the mitotic spindle appeared unaffected.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an observation from immunofluorescence experiments.

claim: Cells expressing Mis12-Ska1 had higher levels of PP1 at kinetochores than control cells expressing either Mis12 or Ska1.
source: Cells expressing Mis12-Ska1 had higher levels of PP1 at kinetochores than control cells expressing either Mis12 or Ska1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1B with quantification.

claim: Expression of Mis12-Ska1 increased PP1 levels at kinetochores in cells treated with nocodazole.
source: Expression of Mis12-Ska1 also increased PP1 levels at kinetochores in cells treated with nocodazole (Figure 1C), suggesting that targeting Ska complex to the kinetochore leads to accumulation of kinetochore PP1 in a microtubule-independent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 1C with quantification.

claim: Targeting Ska complex to the kinetochore leads to accumulation of kinetochore PP1 in a microtubule-independent manner.
source: Expression of Mis12-Ska1 also increased PP1 levels at kinetochores in cells treated with nocodazole (Figure 1C), suggesting that targeting Ska complex to the kinetochore leads to accumulation of kinetochore PP1 in a microtubule-independent manner.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the nocodazole experiment.

claim: Expression of Mis12-Ska1 was not sufficient to accelerate anaphase onset in normal cells.
source: Although expression of Mis12-Ska1 increased PP1 levels at the kinetochore, it was not sufficient to accelerate anaphase onset in normal cells or induce mitotic exit in nocodazole-treated cells (Sivakumar et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: Expression of Mis12-Ska1 was not sufficient to induce mitotic exit in nocodazole-treated cells.
source: Although expression of Mis12-Ska1 increased PP1 levels at the kinetochore, it was not sufficient to accelerate anaphase onset in normal cells or induce mitotic exit in nocodazole-treated cells (Sivakumar et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with a citation to previous work.

claim: Ska3 can be co-immunoprecipitated with PP1 from mitotic HeLa cell lysates.
source: We found that Ska3 could indeed be co-immunoprecipitated (co-IPed) with PP1 (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2A.

claim: Knl1 co-immunoprecipitates with PP1 from mitotic HeLa cell lysates.
source: As a positive control, Knl1, a kinetochore protein known to directly bind PP1 (Liu et al., 2010; Meadows et al., 2011; Rosenberg et al., 2011; Zhang et al., 2014), also co-IPed with PP1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to previous studies.

claim: The Ska complex interacted with similar amounts of PP1 in control and Knl1-depleted cells.
source: The Ska complex interacted with similar amounts of PP1 in control and Knl1-depleted cells.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Knl1 co-immunoprecipitated similar amounts of PP1 from control and Ska3-depleted cells.
source: Knl1 also co-IPed similar amounts of PP1 from control and Ska3-depleted cells, indicating that Ska depletion did not affect the Knl1-PP1 interaction (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2C.

claim: Ska depletion did not affect the Knl1-PP1 interaction.
source: Knl1 also co-IPed similar amounts of PP1 from control and Ska3-depleted cells, indicating that Ska depletion did not affect the Knl1-PP1 interaction (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as an inference from the co-IP experiment.

claim: The Ska complex and Knl1 are capable of independent binding to PP1.
source: From our IP experiments, we conclude that the Ska complex and Knl1 are capable of independent binding to PP1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the co-IP experiments.

claim: GST-Ska1/2 bound efficiently to Myc-PP1 in vitro.
source: GST-Ska1/2 bound efficiently to Myc-PP1, with or without GST-Ska3 (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Ska1/2 physically interacted with PP1 in vitro.
source: Thus, Ska1/2 physically interacted with PP1 in vitro.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the in vitro binding assay.

claim: GFP-Ska1, but not GFP-Ska2 or GFP-Ska3, interacted with mCherry-PP1 in lysates prepared from HeLa cells depleted of the other two endogenous Ska components.
source: We found that GFP-Ska1, but not GFP-Ska2 or GFP-Ska3, interacted with mCherry-PP1 in lysates prepared from HeLa cells depleted of the other two endogenous Ska components (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 2E.

claim: PP1 binding by the Ska complex is mainly mediated by Ska1.
source: Thus, PP1 binding by the Ska complex is mainly mediated by Ska1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the co-IP experiments.

claim: The Ska1 CTD interacted with PP1 in vitro.
source: The Ska1 CTD was found to interact with PP1 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3A.

claim: The Ska complex containing full-length Ska1 bound PP1 in gel-filtration experiments.
source: The Ska complex containing full-length Ska1 bound PP1, while the Ska complex containing Ska1 lacking the CTD showed reduced complex formation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: The Ska complex containing Ska1 lacking the CTD showed reduced complex formation with PP1 in gel-filtration experiments.
source: The Ska complex containing full-length Ska1 bound PP1, while the Ska complex containing Ska1 lacking the CTD showed reduced complex formation (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3B.

claim: Purified recombinant Ska1 CTD and PP1 proteins interacted with a Kd of 1.5 μM.
source: Using microscale thermophoresis, we found that purified recombinant Ska1 CTD and PP1 proteins interacted with a Kd of 1.5 μM (Figure 3C, Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Ska1 CTD and PP1 directly interact with moderate affinity.
source: Thus, Ska1 CTD and PP1 directly interact with moderate affinity.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the MST experiment.

claim: Other parts of Ska or associated proteins may enhance the Ska1 CTD-PP1 interaction in vivo.
source: Other parts of Ska or associated proteins may enhance the Ska1 CTD-PP1 interaction in vivo.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a speculation based on the moderate affinity observed in vitro.

claim: GFP-Ska1 CTD bound to Myc-PP1 in HeLa cells depleted of endogenous Ska complex components.
source: In HeLa cells depleted of endogenous Ska complex components and expressing RNAi-resistant Ska1 fragments, GFP-Ska1 CTD bound to Myc-PP1 (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Exogenously expressed full-length Ska1 localized to centrosomes, spindle microtubules, and kinetochores during mitosis.
source: As reported previously (Abad et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012), exogenously expressed full-length Ska1 localized to centrosomes, spindle microtubules, and kinetochores during mitosis while Ska1ΔCTD localized predominantly to kinetochores (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Ska1ΔCTD localized predominantly to kinetochores during mitosis.
source: As reported previously (Abad et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012), exogenously expressed full-length Ska1 localized to centrosomes, spindle microtubules, and kinetochores during mitosis while Ska1ΔCTD localized predominantly to kinetochores (Figure 4—figure supplement 1).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations and shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1.

claim: Full-length Ska1 interacted more efficiently with endogenous PP1 than did Ska1ΔCTD, with or without depletion of endogenous Ska1.
source: Full-length Ska1 interacted more efficiently with endogenous PP1 than did Ska1ΔCTD, with or without depletion of endogenous Ska1 (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Ska1ΔCTD showed reduced Myc-PP1 binding both in nocodazole- and in MG132-treated cells.
source: Again, Ska1ΔCTD showed reduced Myc-PP1 binding both in nocodazole- and in MG132-treated cells (Figure 4C-figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 4C and Figure 4—figure supplement 2.

claim: PP1 localization to the kinetochore was decreased by 50% in cells expressing Ska1ΔCTD, compared to cells expressing full-length Ska1.
source: PP1 localization to the kinetochore was decreased by 50% in cells expressing Ska1ΔCTD, compared to cells expressing full-length Ska1 (Figure 5A), with or without depletion of Ska1.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5A with quantification.

claim: Ska1ΔCTD could diminish PP1 kinetochore targeting in a dominant negative fashion.
source: Thus, Ska1ΔCTD could diminish PP1 kinetochore targeting in a dominant negative fashion, confirming a role for the Ska1 CTD in PP1 targeting to kinetochores.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the immunofluorescence experiment.

claim: Mps1 phosphorylates Knl1 on multiple MELT motifs.
source: The spindle checkpoint kinase Mps1 phosphorylates Knl1 on multiple MELT motifs, and the phosphorylated MELT recruits other checkpoint components, such as Bub1, to kinetochores (Yamagishi et al., 2012; Shepperd et al., 2012; London et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to previous studies.

claim: Phosphorylated MELT motifs recruit checkpoint components, such as Bub1, to kinetochores.
source: The spindle checkpoint kinase Mps1 phosphorylates Knl1 on multiple MELT motifs, and the phosphorylated MELT recruits other checkpoint components, such as Bub1, to kinetochores (Yamagishi et al., 2012; Shepperd et al., 2012; London et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to previous studies.

claim: Phosphorylation of pMELT (residue pT875) was elevated in cells expressing Ska1ΔCTD, as compared to cells expressing full-length Ska1.
source: We found that phosphorylation of one such MELT motif, pMELT (residue pT875), was indeed elevated in cells expressing Ska1ΔCTD, as compared to cells expressing full-length Ska1 (Figure 5B) (Ji et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5B with quantification.

claim: Cells expressing Ska1ΔCTD showed increased levels of Bub1 protein at kinetochores, as compared to cells expressing full-length Ska1.
source: Consistent with this finding, cells expressing Ska1ΔCTD showed increased levels of Bub1 protein at kinetochores, as compared to cells expressing full-length Ska1 (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 5C with quantification.

claim: PP1 recruited by the Ska1 CTD opposes Knl1 phosphorylation by Mps1 directly or indirectly.
source: These results indicate that PP1 recruited by the Ska1 CTD opposes Knl1 phosphorylation by Mps1 directly or indirectly.
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the pMELT and Bub1 experiments.

claim: PP1 depletion causes delays at metaphase.
source: PP1 depletion was found to cause delays at metaphase (Liu et al., 2010; Nijenhuis et al., 2014; Zhang et al., 2014).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations to previous studies.

claim: Expression of RNAi-resistant Ska1 rescued the arrest caused by Ska1 depletion.
source: As expected, expression of RNAi-resistant Ska1 rescued the arrest caused by Ska1 depletion (Figure 6A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Expression of Ska1ΔCTD did not rescue the metaphase arrest/delay caused by Ska1 depletion.
source: Consistent with previous reports (Abad et al., 2014; Schmidt et al., 2012), expression of Ska1ΔCTD did not rescue the metaphase arrest/delay caused by Ska1 depletion (Figure 6A,B).
evidence: This is stated in the results section with citations and shown in Figure 6A,B.

claim: Expression of Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81) fusion in Ska1-depleted cells rescued metaphase arrest.
source: Expression of Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81) fusion in Ska1-depleted cells rescued metaphase arrest while expression of Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81)4A did not.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Expression of Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81)4A did not rescue metaphase arrest in Ska1-depleted cells.
source: Expression of Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81) fusion in Ska1-depleted cells rescued metaphase arrest while expression of Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81)4A did not.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6A.

claim: Expression of Ska1ΔCTD caused dominant negative effects in delaying mitotic progression in cells not depleted of endogenous Ska1.
source: In cells not depleted of endogenous Ska1, dominant negative effects in delaying mitotic progression were caused by expression of Ska1ΔCTD, as previously reported, and by expression of the fusion Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81)4A, which lacks the PP1-binding motif.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Expression of Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81)4A caused dominant negative effects in delaying mitotic progression in cells not depleted of endogenous Ska1.
source: In cells not depleted of endogenous Ska1, dominant negative effects in delaying mitotic progression were caused by expression of Ska1ΔCTD, as previously reported, and by expression of the fusion Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81)4A, which lacks the PP1-binding motif.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: Expression of Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81) but not Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81)4A showed significant rescue of the delay caused by Ska1 depletion.
source: Expression of Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81) but not Ska1ΔCTDKnl1(34–81)4A showed significant rescue of the delay caused by Ska1 depletion.
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 6B.

claim: The decreased PP1 recruitment contributes to the Ska depletion phenotype.
source: This result suggests that the decreased PP1 recruitment contributes to the Ska depletion phenotype (Figure 6A–C).
evidence: This is stated in the results section as a conclusion from the rescue experiments.

claim: Expression of the Ska1-PP1 chimeric protein produced higher PP1 accumulation (1.5-fold increase) at kinetochores.
source: Gratifyingly, expression of the Ska1-PP1 chimeric protein produced higher PP1 accumulation (1.5-fold increase) at kinetochores (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and resulted in complete rescue of the mitotic arrest and alignment delay phenotypes and substantially reduced the metaphase delay phenotype induced by Ska1 depletion (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7—figure supplement 1.

claim: Expression of the Ska1-PP1 chimeric protein resulted in complete rescue of the mitotic arrest phenotype induced by Ska1 depletion.
source: Gratifyingly, expression of the Ska1-PP1 chimeric protein produced higher PP1 accumulation (1.5-fold increase) at kinetochores (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and resulted in complete rescue of the mitotic arrest and alignment delay phenotypes and substantially reduced the metaphase delay phenotype induced by Ska1 depletion (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Expression of the Ska1-PP1 chimeric protein resulted in complete rescue of the alignment delay phenotype induced by Ska1 depletion.
source: Gratifyingly, expression of the Ska1-PP1 chimeric protein produced higher PP1 accumulation (1.5-fold increase) at kinetochores (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and resulted in complete rescue of the mitotic arrest and alignment delay phenotypes and substantially reduced the metaphase delay phenotype induced by Ska1 depletion (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7A.

claim: Expression of the Ska1-PP1 chimeric protein substantially reduced the metaphase delay phenotype induced by Ska1 depletion.
source: Gratifyingly, expression of the Ska1-PP1 chimeric protein produced higher PP1 accumulation (1.5-fold increase) at kinetochores (Figure 7—figure supplement 1), and resulted in complete rescue of the mitotic arrest and alignment delay phenotypes and substantially reduced the metaphase delay phenotype induced by Ska1 depletion (Figure 7A).
evidence: This is stated in the results section and shown in Figure 7A.
